refresh_caller_completion_review.historical_reason: A lost transition can suspend before release forever; bound and diagnose each gate.
refresh_caller_completion_review.historical_assessment: Original gate/synchronization notes remain revision-bound historical evidence. This nine-rule block reviews the current caller-outcome observation change.

rules.1: Both send outcomes retain HTTP 200, one refresh, zero mid-token sends, two final-token sends and stored final credentials. Each completion actor is signaled only after the actual send/recovery call returns or throws; original response and typed-error assertions remain.
rules.2: Use separate existing completion actors for originator and joiner, observed concurrently with source-located stage diagnostics. Only proven outcomes permit task-value awaits. Existing refresh/mid-save/initial-send gates and release order remain unchanged.
rules.3: Existing ten-second failure budget per completion actor, concurrent observations; no latency assertion or sleep used as readiness.
rules.4: On missing outcome, release all fake gates, request cancellation of both handles and return without awaiting unconfirmed work. This does not prove stuck task termination; asynchronous drainage remains open when unproven.
rules.5: Fresh in-memory credential store, fake transport, coordinator and two independent single-waiter completion actors; synthetic account/tokens only.
rules.6: Host-local deterministic auth integration with fake HTTP transport; no production or transport redesign.
rules.7: No retry-to-green or reduced assertion strength; success and typed negative outcomes remain consumed from their original task handles after completion proof.
rules.8: New completion diagnostics contain only missing caller stage and elapsed timeout. Caught operation errors are rethrown unchanged; no result/token payload is added to those diagnostics.
rules.9: Reviewed the existing bounded completion helper for one waiter per actor and the three tests. Repeated, owning and signed evidence is linked.

refresh_caller_completion_review.execution: Three independent focused passes 3/3 each, owning 24/24, signed host 592/592 and exact discovery 592; zero failures/errors/skips. Strict Swift lint, docs and diff checks passed.

token_response_lifecycle_review.historical_assessment: Original notes remain revision-bound; this nine-rule block reviews the current controlled-response/caller-observation slice.

rules.1: Observe acquiring availability while an explicitly held token response is pending, then bound actual acquisition return. Original availability, typed-error and cancellation-count assertions remain.
rules.2: Existing entry/challenge signals, controlled response, bounded caller completion and retirement replace timed holds. Existing actor count proves sole-waiter removal before retirement.
rules.3: Remove five/thirty-second success-capable fake holds from these cases. Existing ten-second deadlines report missing transition/release/exit; no latency assertion or readiness sleep.
rules.4: Await existing withTestCleanup on normal/throwing exits: cancel caller, disable provider, retire response. Task values require actual caller-result proof; cleanup never awaits unconfirmed handles. Whole underlying graph drainage is not claimed.
rules.5: Fresh fake attester, memory enrollment store, provider, response gate and separate single-waiter completion actor; synthetic data only.
rules.6: Host fake transport integration. Retirement releases the response and checks actual Task.isCancelled; retirement itself does not cancel that task.
rules.7: Measure genuine cancellation before cleanup disables the provider; no retry-to-green or relaxed error criteria.
rules.8: Source-located caller completion and existing retirement diagnostics; the typed-result helper preserves values/errors without adding token payloads to new diagnostics.
rules.9: Reviewed existing result/completion/cleanup/retirement helpers, synchronous waiter removal/cancel ordering, and all three callers; execution evidence linked.

token_response_lifecycle_review.historical_assessment: Original notes remain revision-bound; this nine-rule block reviews the current controlled-response/caller-observation slice.

rules.1: Retain exact cancelled error, genuine transport cancellation signal and cancellation count 1; observe last-waiter removal before response retirement and measure cancellation before cleanup disables the provider. Original availability, typed-error and cancellation-count assertions remain.
rules.2: Existing entry/challenge signals, controlled response, bounded caller completion and retirement replace timed holds. Existing actor count proves sole-waiter removal before retirement.
rules.3: Remove five/thirty-second success-capable fake holds from these cases. Existing ten-second deadlines report missing transition/release/exit; no latency assertion or readiness sleep.
rules.4: Await existing withTestCleanup on normal/throwing exits: cancel caller, disable provider, retire response. Task values require actual caller-result proof; cleanup never awaits unconfirmed handles. Whole underlying graph drainage is not claimed.
rules.5: Fresh fake attester, memory enrollment store, provider, response gate and separate single-waiter completion actor; synthetic data only.
rules.6: Host fake transport integration. Retirement releases the response and checks actual Task.isCancelled; retirement itself does not cancel that task.
rules.7: Measure genuine cancellation before cleanup disables the provider; no retry-to-green or relaxed error criteria.
rules.8: Source-located caller completion and existing retirement diagnostics; the typed-result helper preserves values/errors without adding token payloads to new diagnostics.
rules.9: Reviewed existing result/completion/cleanup/retirement helpers, synchronous waiter removal/cancel ordering, and all three callers; execution evidence linked.
